title: Towards a Theory of Quantitative Vulnerability Analysis for Engineering Systems
summary: Since the 1980s, risk analysis for engineering systems has been defined based on a tuple of scenarios, $\mathcal{S}$, likelihoods, $L$, and consequences, $C$, where $Risk = (\mathcal{S},L,C)$. We argue that equating this triplet with risk alone is insufficient and potentially misleading. Instead, we define this tuple as a vulnerability space $\mathcal{V} = (\mathcal{S},L,C)$, which becomes risk only when one makes specific interpretations of likelihood and consequence.
